clue.text: One might give money for canine toy for Thai mongrel

definitions.text: One might give money for canine

indicators.note: a mongrel is a mixed breed, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog toy bought for a Thai mutt, as if a pet-shop purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like the dog of the surface, but here it is a canine tooth, which children leave under the pillow for a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore figure who leaves a coin in exchange for a child's lost tooth, canines included.

clue.text: Part-time worker left eastern place of worship

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker

explanation.surface: A temp has quit a job at an oriental shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like the verb quit, but it is the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A building for religious worship, especially in non-Christian faiths.

clue.text: Control rebellious bosses

indicators.note: rebellious letters refuse their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to rein in managers who have rebelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To preoccupy the mind completely is to dominate or control one's thoughts.

clue.text: Inuit sauce he mixed, producing top-quality cooking

indicators.note: mixing stirs things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef mixes an Inuit sauce and serves fine dining.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for elaborate gourmet cuisine, literally high cooking.

clue.text: Displays locks in the East End?

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their aitches, so the opening H goes

parts.note: locks of hair are hairs

explanation.surface: Showing off one's hair in a working-class London district.
explanation.walkthrough: London's East End is home of the Cockney accent, which drops H.
explanation.definitionFit: Puts on affected manners or shows off, as in putting on airs and graces.

clue.text: Vegetable greed — madly purchasing one hundred and four Swedes?

indicators.note: purchasing means taking in, so the rearranged letters hold the next pieces
madly means wildly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is one hundred in Roman numerals
ABBA were a Swedish pop group of four members

explanation.surface: Greedy shoppers buying up turnip-like swedes by the hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swedes' looks like the vegetable (a turnip) but is the four Swedish members of ABBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple-leaved variety of cabbage, a common vegetable.

clue.text: River following low ground covered with heath?

indicators.note: the river's letter comes after the cattle sound, so it is placed second

parts.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes, moo

explanation.surface: A river runs past a low-lying patch of heathland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective for the ground, but it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Open upland largely covered in heather and heath is what this landscape word describes.

clue.text: Ran over and talked foolishly about European

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the foolish-talk word goes about, around, the European letter

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly, so prated

explanation.surface: Someone overran and babbled nonsense about a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' is in the sense of ran a business or machine.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a machine or business is to work or manage it.

clue.text: Book of the Bible with reduced description of Herod?

parts.note: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament
less means reduced in amount

explanation.surface: A Bible book with a cut-down account of King Herod.
explanation.walkthrough: Herod ordered the massacre of the innocents, so 'merciless' suits him; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod was notoriously cruel and pitiless, so merciless is an apt adjective for him.

clue.text: A dream Sue reconstructed about queen's fancy-dress party

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the queen's letter, holding it inside
something reconstructed is rebuilt in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Q is the abbreviation for queen, as on playing cards

explanation.surface: Someone named Sue rebuilds a dream about a queen holding a costume party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstructed' rearranges A DREAM SUE, and 'about' wraps those letters round Q.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball or party where guests come in costumes and masks is this kind of event.

clue.text: 'Relacher' primarily is French for 'relax'

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: in French 'is' is est

explanation.surface: A language lesson: the French verb relacher means to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is French' is not a statement about the word but a request to put 'is' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a break and unwind is a plain synonym of relax.

clue.text: Wandering, having gone off?

parts.note: someone who has gone off (dropped off to sleep) yet wanders about is moving around while unconscious

explanation.walkthrough: 'gone off' reads as left, but here means fallen asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking about while asleep, a sleep disorder called somnambulism.

clue.text: In school, is tending to pay attention

indicators.note: the letters sit in the run of words that follows, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: A school report: the pupil is beginning to pay attention in class.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend closely to what is said, especially with the ears, is to pay attention.

clue.text: Boris Johnson captivates everyone with a couple of lines somewhere in London

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold, so the leader's letters hold the next piece inside

parts.note: Boris Johnson was British Prime Minister, PM
everyone means all
L is short for line, so two of them make LL

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister charms everyone with a few lines somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: PALL MALL is a street in London's St James's, near the clubs and palaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known street in central London, so a vague place in the capital fits it.

clue.text: Put up with stage's position

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate it
a point is a stage, as in at this point; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: Tolerating a theatre stage's placement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' is not the theatre platform but a point in a process.
explanation.definitionFit: A point of view or attitude is one's position on an issue.

clue.text: Introduction to sport: it enables us to develop fitness

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the word is used
to develop is to change form, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A sport primer promising that it will help us get fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitness' is not physical fitness here but appropriateness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being appropriate or apt for a purpose is fitness in its sense of suitability.

clue.text: Changing a pillow on rising can end in suffering

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the cushion word is reversed

parts.note: a pad is a cushion or pillow
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the end of the word means its final letter

explanation.surface: Changing a pillow when getting up can stop the suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering or adjusting to suit new conditions is changing.

clue.text: Incomparable description of the House of Lords at the end of the day?

definitions.text: description of the House of Lords at the end of the day?
definitions.meaning: once members go home, the chamber is without its nobles

explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is Britain's upper chamber, whose members are peers.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no equal means being unmatched, which is incomparable.

clue.text: Telling-off good for one daughter making loose garment

indicators.note: one thing for another means a swap, so the good letter replaces the daughter's

parts.note: a dressing-down is a severe scolding
D is the abbreviation for daughter; one says only one D changes

explanation.surface: A daughter gets scolded, and something good comes of it in the form of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the two Ds in DRESSING DOWN, it is the one starting DOWN that becomes G.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose robe worn over nightclothes around the house is this garment.

clue.text: Rub smooth tongue

definitions.meaning: a tongue is a language, here the language of Poland

explanation.definitionFit: To shine by rubbing, and also the language spoken in Poland.

clue.text: Think rationally about a relative

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: Advice to think logically about a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: To use logic to reach conclusions is to think rationally.

clue.text: Endlessly cut and cut small food items

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
to snip is to cut with scissors
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Chopping vegetables over and over into little pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'cut's must be read as verbs supplying different synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Root vegetables eaten as food, so plural edible things fits them.

clue.text: Opening a chapter in deep affection

indicators.note: the chapter letter is put inside the word for affection

parts.note: deep affection is love

explanation.surface: A romance novel's opening chapter steeped in tender feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like the start of a book, but it means a recess in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess or niche set back into a wall is an opening in it.

clue.text: Small portion — this writer eats it

indicators.note: eating takes something in, so the writer's word holds the other inside

parts.note: this writer is the setter, me

explanation.surface: The setter admits to eating a small serving.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount or a small contribution, as in the widow's mite.

clue.text: I bumped into flipping object

indicators.note: flipping turns something over, so the word for meeting is read backwards

parts.note: to bump into someone is to meet them, met

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker who walked into some blasted thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' poses as a mild British swear word in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A single article or thing is an object.

clue.text: Six municipalities including Northern Ireland's surrounding areas

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the municipal word includes, holding inside, the Northern Ireland letters

parts.note: cities are municipalities
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Six councils in Northern Ireland and the districts around them.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland, the part of the UK on the island of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Neighbourhoods round about a place are its surroundings, so the plural fits surrounding areas.

clue.text: Talk then quietly catch one's breath

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
P stands for piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Someone chats away, then pauses quietly to breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp sudden intake of breath, in shock or effort, is to catch one's breath.

clue.text: Drunk gets thinner — not one to beef up

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled
not marks a letter as missing, so the one letter is left out of the jumble

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A drinker who has lost weight, though not enough to build any muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' says to remove I from GETS THINNER before 'Drunk' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef up is to make more robust, a direct synonym.
